2026-09-16. Recorded under the r11 closure mandate's AFK review authority on explicit owner

DEPENDENCY-ONLY RE-AFFIRMATION. This root's own claim text, security consequence, scope,
owner and review requirement are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the reviewed version; `theorem_claim` is
unchanged and only `theorem_dependencies` moved. What moved, and why each is a CLAIM
CORRECTION bringing the registry to what the code already does — no implementation was
weakened by any of them:

(1) THM-0062 statement. It claimed the response signer yields no credential "when its
    snapshot lock is poisoned". `current` recovers poison with
    `unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())` and then applies only `now < a.exp`; the snapshot is
    one `Option<Arc<..>>` swapped whole, so no partially mutated invariant can become visible
    and a poisoned lock is observationally identical to a healthy one. The theorem's own
    cited control asserted the opposite of the theorem. The statement now says terminal
    retirement dominates every later read, that poison is RECOVERED because the protected
    state is whole-value, and that recovery overrides neither retirement nor expiration. The
    terminal-retirement guarantee is unchanged. The misnamed control was renamed in the same
    slice to `a_poisoned_snapshot_lock_is_recovered_and_retirement_still_dominates`.

(2) THM-0048 statement, security_consequence and scope. It claimed "a rebuild with withdrawn
    trust advances the epoch and stops resumption". Anchors are immutable for a listener's
    lifetime and `bind_resumption` hands `republish` the epoch the store already holds, so
    that branch never fires on any build path — and THM-0103's scope already disclaimed the
    same proposition. Owner ruling: OPTION A, do not reopen live trust-anchor rotation to make
    old prose true; ADR-MCPRE-062, superseding ADR-MCPRE-055, chose the replacement/restart
    model and the code implements it. The statement now says a replacement listener and
    session-cache boundary does not carry resumption authority across the replacement when the
    epoch differs; the consequence is bounded to ACROSS THE REPLACEMENT; and the scope states
    the operator obligation that changing the trust-anchor set requires listener replacement
    or restart for the new epoch to become authoritative. The store-level control was renamed
    to `republishing_a_different_epoch_supersedes_the_stores_sessions` so it can no longer be
    read as evidence for a listener-level advance it cannot observe.

(3) THM-0027 scope. It disclaimed an escape hatch through
    `TlsListenerSecurityState::build_delegated_resolver_config` that no longer exists — the
    function became private in a50d4070 (#886) and its one caller goes through `materialize`.
    The paragraph was vacuous and read as permission to reopen one. It now states positively
    that within the API this crate publishes there is no route bypassing the validated
    correspondence gate, while keeping the embedder boundary explicitly outside the claim.
    Statement and security_consequence are unchanged.

(4) THM-0087 title, security_consequence and scope. "Reachable" did not say what it
    quantifies over. It now says: through MCP-RE's continuation read/remove authority. A party
    with direct write access to the `mcp-re:cont:` keyspace falls outside the quantifier — it
    plants its own entry under its own actor's key — and that is ASM-0047, already registered
    against this theorem in verification/generated/assumption-consumers.md, with ASM-0048
    carrying the `DEL` one-shot count and the `PX` bound. The edit puts an already-registered
    premise into the theorem's own words. R11-346's code closure was already fixed.

(5) A NEW assumption, ASM-0049, registers the premise THM-0103's epoch equality rested on and
    that no entry stated: two distinct trust-anchor sets this deployment admits produce
    distinct SHA-256 epoch digests. Owner ruling: OPTION 1, the narrow sibling. ASM-0037 was
    deliberately NOT widened — the operator chooses both anchor sets and the adversary chooses
    neither, so the premise is weaker than collision resistance and weaker than
    second-preimage, and naming ASM-0037 here would report a premise stronger than the claim
    needs. Nothing here assumes or claims SHA-256 collision resistance for this unit.

Each edit was read against the source before it was made. No conjunct of this root was
broadened: (1)-(4) each NARROW or restate a registered claim to what its evidence reaches,
and (5) adds a premise that was previously unstated, which makes the trusted-premise set
larger and the claim no more than it was.
